$comment: The origin of a knowledge base's gateway, made from its HTTP endpoint, as every SDK must make it: what a session sends its requests to and opens its stream at. TypeScript (`kbGatewayUrl`, @semiont/sdk), Rust (`HttpEndpoint::gateway_url`, semiont) and Python (`gateway_url`, semiont.http) each run every case and fail on a difference. A host is a host's name or it is refused, and a refused host is never put into a URL: a host's name is labels of ASCII letters, digits and hyphens with a dot between each two, every label 1 to 63 characters long and none beginning or ending with a hyphen. A dotted address and `localhost` are such names; a host with a slash, a colon, a space, a query, a bracket or a letter outside ASCII is not. The origin is the protocol, `://`, the host in lowercase and nothing else done to it, `:` and the port, written even when it is the protocol's own. READING A CASE. `endpoint` is an HttpEndpoint (components/schemas/HttpEndpoint.json), and `origin` the gateway's origin, or null when the host is refused.

cases.why: a host's name is put in lowercase, and the port is written even when it is the protocol's own
a dotted address is a host's name, kept as it is written
a host of digits alone is a name like any other: it is kept as it is written, not read as an address
a hyphen inside a label is a name's
a label of 63 characters is a label
an empty host is no name
a path is no part of a host
a port is no part of a host
a query is no part of a host
a label does not begin with a hyphen
a label does not end with a hyphen
a label is not empty, between two dots
a label is not empty, after a last dot
a space is no part of a name
a label of 64 characters is too long
a letter outside ASCII is no part of a name
an address in brackets is no name
